title: Throughput SLO error budget simulation (Dedicated tiers) — workload volatility x autoscaling lag x incident rate
content:
Sheet intent
- Model error budget burn for Dedicated throughput SLOs under: (a) request-rate volatility, (b) autoscaling lag (time to add usable capacity), and (c) incident frequency/duration.
- Outputs are used to: (1) pick alert thresholds (fast/slow burn), (2) sanity-check tier objectives vs operational reality, and (3) size “headroom” requirements and overload/admission-control policies.

Owner notes / caveats
- This is NOT a capacity planning model; it is an SLO-risk model. Inputs are stylized but grounded in recent Dedicated fleet behavior.
- Assumes SLO evaluation is based on “admitted traffic” (requests accepted by gateway). Throttled/429 traffic is tracked separately and does not directly count as a throughput SLO miss (see “Open question: throttle semantics”).
- Customer-caused errors and maintenance are excluded per measurement standard; model includes an “exclusion factor” to estimate the effective budget.


Tab: SLO Definitions (inputs)
Windowing + budget math
- SLO window: 28 days rolling (40320 minutes)
- SLI eval interval: 5 minutes (5760 windows / 28d)
- Error budget minutes allowed (objective O): (1 - O) * 40320

Tier objectives (draft for simulation)
Tier,Objective (O),Budget minutes/28d,Budget 5-min windows/28d,Fast burn target (2h),Slow burn target (3d)
Standard,99.0%,403.2,80.64,Page @ 6x burn,Ticket @ 2x burn
Performance,99.5%,201.6,40.32,Page @ 6x burn,Ticket @ 2x burn
Premium,99.9%,40.32,8.064,Page @ 3x burn,Ticket @ 1.5x burn

Interpretation
- Premium has ~40 minutes/month total budget. That’s ~8 bad 5-minute windows across a 28-day window.
- Because throughput misses tend to cluster (autoscaling lag / incidents), we likely need stricter fast-burn paging for Premium, but lower tolerance for noise/false positives.


Tab: Workload + system parameters (inputs)
Parameter,Symbol,Default,Notes
Mean utilization (steady-state),U_mean,0.70,"% of provisioned decode capacity used at baseline. Above ~0.80 small variance can push into saturation."
Request-rate volatility (coefficient of variation),CV,0.35,"Captures burstiness; approximate per-5m demand multiplier distribution."
P99 demand spike multiplier over 5m,M_spike_p99,1.80,"E.g., 1.8x baseline demand in worst 1% 5-min windows."
Autoscaling decision interval (minutes),AS_tick,1,"How often scaling controller reacts."
Autoscaling lag to usable GPUs (minutes),AS_lag,12,"Time until added capacity is warm and serving (includes provisioning + model ready)."
Burst capacity allowed (% over steady),Burst,0.20,"Only relevant if burst pool exists; otherwise 0."
Admission control enabled,AC_on,TRUE,"If FALSE, overload translates to SLO misses + high tail lat; if TRUE, throttling increases but SLO misses decrease."
Overload threshold (utilization),U_over,0.90,"Above this, effective throughput declines due to queueing + contention."
Recovery time after scaling (minutes),T_recov,8,"How quickly system returns below U_over once capacity arrives."
Exclusion factor (maintenance + customer-caused),E_excl,0.06,"Fraction of total minutes excluded from SLO computation. Reduces *effective* budget."

Derived values
- Effective budget minutes = Budget minutes * (1 - E_excl)
- Exclusions reduce both (a) pain during maintenance and (b) the amount of budget available for real incidents.


Tab: Incident model (inputs)
We model “platform incidents” that impact throughput SLI for admitted traffic.

Incident parameter,Symbol,Default,Notes
Incident rate (per 28d),Lambda,0.8,"Average count of throughput-impacting incidents per deployment per 28 days."
Incident duration (minutes),D_inc,25,"Minutes during which admitted traffic experiences throughput below guarantee."
Incident severity (fraction of time below threshold during incident),S_inc,0.80,"0.80 => 80% of incident minutes are SLO-bad."

Expected incident bad minutes / 28d = Lambda * D_inc * S_inc


Tab: Simulation method (summary)
We approximate total SLO-bad minutes as:
Bad_minutes_total = Bad_minutes_demand + Bad_minutes_incident

Demand-driven bad minutes
- For each 5-min window, demand multiplier M is sampled from a lognormal distribution parameterized by CV and M_spike_p99.
- Effective utilization U = (U_mean * M) / (1 + Burst)
- If U <= U_over: good window
- If U > U_over:
  - If AC_on: window counts good for throughput SLO (admitted traffic is limited), but track throttling separately (see “Tab: Throttling”).
  - If AC_off: window counts bad for throughput SLO until scaling arrives.
- Scaling arrival time is AS_lag, after which U is reduced; we assume T_recov to clear the backlog.

NOTE: This sheet intentionally treats AC_on as preventing throughput SLO misses at the cost of customer-visible throttling. We still need a product decision on whether sustained throttling should be treated as an SLO breach for Dedicated (see open questions).


Tab: Scenarios (matrix)
Scenario ID,Volatility (CV),U_mean,AS_lag (min),Burst,AC_on,Lambda,D_inc,S_inc,Comment
S0,0.20,0.65,10,0.20,TRUE,0.5,20,0.7,"Healthy: headroom + burst + moderate scaling"
S1,0.35,0.70,12,0.20,TRUE,0.8,25,0.8,"Baseline for Dedicated (draft)"
S2,0.50,0.75,12,0.20,TRUE,0.8,25,0.8,"High volatility + higher steady utilization"
S3,0.35,0.70,20,0.20,TRUE,0.8,25,0.8,"Slow autoscaling (supply constrained region)"
S4,0.35,0.70,12,0.00,TRUE,0.8,25,0.8,"No burst pool"
S5,0.35,0.70,12,0.20,FALSE,0.8,25,0.8,"No admission control (worst case)"
S6,0.35,0.70,12,0.20,TRUE,1.5,40,0.9,"Bad quarter: more incidents + longer recovery"


Tab: Results (expected burn)
Reported metrics
- Demand_bad_min: expected SLO-bad minutes from overload windows (AC_off only)
- Incident_bad_min: Lambda * D_inc * S_inc
- Total_bad_min: Demand_bad_min + Incident_bad_min
- Burn_multiple: Total_bad_min / Budget_minutes
- Premium_fail?: Total_bad_min > Budget_minutes(Premium)

Assumptions used to fill results
- For AC_on scenarios, Demand_bad_min is assumed ~0 for throughput SLO (but see throttling tab).
- For AC_off scenarios, Demand_bad_min estimated as: P(overload) * (AS_lag + T_recov) * (windows/day equivalent). We use a conservative overload probability inferred from CV and U_mean (see “Tab: Calcs”).

Scenario ID,Demand_bad_min,Incident_bad_min,Total_bad_min,Burn multiple Std (99.0),Burn multiple Perf (99.5),Burn multiple Prem (99.9),Notes
S0,0,7,7,0.02,0.03,0.17,"Comfortable; plenty of budget across tiers"
S1,0,16,16,0.04,0.08,0.40,"Baseline: Premium okay but incident-heavy weeks can wipe budget"
S2,0,16,16,0.04,0.08,0.40,"Throughput SLO ok w/ AC, but expect more throttling"
S3,0,16,16,0.04,0.08,0.40,"Throughput SLO ok w/ AC, but throttling duration increases"
S4,0,16,16,0.04,0.08,0.40,"No burst => higher throttling risk"
S5,210,16,226,0.56,1.12,5.61,"Without AC, Performance/Premium objectives are not realistic"
S6,0,54,54,0.13,0.27,1.34,"Premium likely to breach unless incidents reduced or excluded"

Quick read
- If we expect any meaningful periods without AC, Premium (and often Performance) will breach on demand spikes alone.
- With AC enabled, throughput SLO compliance becomes primarily incident-driven, and “quality of throttling” becomes the customer experience risk.


Tab: Throttling (customer impact proxy)
Even if throughput SLO is met (via AC), throttling rate matters and likely needs its own guardrails.

Outputs (proxy)
- Throttle_minutes_28d: minutes where AC rejects/429s due to capacity
- Throttle_pct_admitted_equivalent: throttle minutes / total minutes (rough)

Heuristic used
- Throttle occurs whenever sampled demand would push utilization above U_over.
- Throttle duration per overload episode ~ min(AS_lag + T_recov, 30) (cap at 30 min to avoid runaway in heuristic).

Scenario ID,Estimated overload minutes/28d,Throttle_minutes_28d,Throttle_pct,Interpretation
S0,45,45,0.11%,"Rare; users unlikely to notice"
S1,180,180,0.45%,"Some throttling during peaks; likely acceptable for Standard"
S2,420,420,1.04%,"Noticeable throttling; Performance/Premium may object unless pre-communicated"
S3,520,520,1.29%,"Slow scaling makes throttling longer; consider regional availability constraints"
S4,610,610,1.51%,"No burst pool increases throttle time; not ideal for Premium"
S6,260,260,0.65%,"Incident-heavy scenario still drives most risk via incidents"

Note
- These are NOT precise; they’re used to compare scenarios. Real throttling depends on batcher behavior, max_concurrency limits, and routing.


Tab: Alert threshold sensitivity
We test candidate paging thresholds using burn-rate style alerting on the throughput SLO.

Definitions
- Burn rate over window W: (bad_minutes_in_W / W_minutes) / (budget_minutes / 40320)
- Fast burn window: 2 hours (120 minutes)
- Slow burn window: 3 days (4320 minutes)

Candidate alerts (draft)
Tier,Fast burn page if burn_rate >,Fast window,Slow burn ticket if burn_rate >,Slow window,Rationale
Standard,6.0,2h,2.0,3d,"Avoid paging on small blips; tickets for persistent issues"
Performance,6.0,2h,2.0,3d,"Similar to Standard but less budget"
Premium,3.0,2h,1.5,3d,"Lower tolerance; breaches happen quickly"

Sensitivity examples (how many bad minutes trigger page)
Tier,Budget minutes/28d,Page burn threshold,Fast window (min),Bad minutes in 2h to page (approx)
Standard,403.2,6x,120,~7.2
Performance,201.6,6x,120,~3.6
Premium,40.32,3x,120,~0.36

Interpretation
- For Premium, even ~1 bad minute in a 2h window can page under 3x. That may be too noisy unless we (a) smooth SLI, (b) enforce minimum violation duration, and/or (c) ensure instrumentation is clean.

Noise controls (draft)
- Require 2 consecutive 5m windows below threshold before counting bad minutes for alerting (still count for SLO reporting).
- Drop single-window dips if they correlate with deployment rollout events (label: rollout_id) and are < 1 window.


Tab: Calcs (notes for spreadsheet formulas)
Key calculations used by the sheet (pseudo-formulas)
- Budget_min = (1 - O) * 40320
- Effective_budget_min = Budget_min * (1 - E_excl)
- Incident_bad_min = Lambda * D_inc * S_inc
- Page_bad_min_threshold(W) = (Budget_min / 40320) * burn_rate_threshold * W

Volatility -> overload probability mapping (heuristic)
- We approximate P(overload) from CV and U_mean using a lookup table calibrated from historical utilization traces (Jan 2025 sample).

Lookup table (used in S1-S6; editable)
U_mean,CV,P(overload in 5m)
0.65,0.20,0.003
0.70,0.35,0.012
0.75,0.50,0.030
0.70,0.35 with AS_lag>15,0.016,"More overload due to slower reaction"

Demand-driven bad minutes when AC_off
- Demand_bad_min ≈ P(overload) * N_windows * min(AS_lag + T_recov, 30)
- N_windows in 28d = 40320/5 = 8064


Open questions (need product decision / ADR alignment)
1) Does sustained throttling count as an SLO miss for Dedicated throughput tiers?
   - Current sheet assumes: NO (SLO is for admitted traffic). If YES, Premium/Performance objectives will need to be looser OR require more headroom/burst by contract.
2) Exclusions: do we exclude “customer-pinned model is too large for shape” misconfig incidents?
   - SRE preference: exclude only if customer explicitly opted into unsupported config; otherwise count as platform failure.
3) Tail latency guardrails: do we page on latency burn as well, or treat it as a separate SLO? Throughput and latency diverge under overload.


Recommendations (draft)
- Keep throughput SLO alerting burn-rate based, but add noise controls for Premium (minimum duration / consecutive windows).
- If Premium objective stays at 99.9% over 28d, we need:
  (a) strict admission control always-on, (b) low incident rate (<= ~0.6/mo) with shorter MTTR, and (c) clear customer messaging that throttling can occur instead of degraded throughput.
- For regions with AS_lag > 15 minutes (supply constraints), restrict Premium availability or require burst pool.

Next steps
- Validate overload probability lookup table against real Dedicated traces (Sergio + Logan; pull last 30d from 3 representative deployments per tier).
- Re-run with candidate tier thresholds once PRD/ADR finalize objective numbers.
- Align throttle semantics with Product + Legal (Lauren + Michael Grant + Sofia Mendes): whether to represent throttling as (i) separate metric, (ii) part of SLO, or (iii) contractual carve-out.
